title: Reef fish minimum sizes (snapper, grouper, hogfish, amberjacks, triggerfish, sea bass, red porgy)
effect: Sets the state minimum size for each reef fish, in total length for snappers, groupers, black sea bass and red porgy, and fork length for amberjacks, gray triggerfish and hogfish.
excerpt: No person shall land, possess, unnecessarily destroy, purchase, exchange, sell or offer for sale any of the following species harvested in or from state waters, of a length less than set forth as follows:
full: Values read from the 26 Oct 2023 text (summarised list, not quoted): gag and black grouper 24 in TL; red, yellowfin, yellowmouth grouper 20 in TL; scamp 20 in TL Atlantic and Monroe, 16 in TL Gulf; goliath 24 to 36 in TL; hogfish 16 in FL Atlantic and south of 25 deg 09 min N, 14 in FL north; greater amberjack 28 in FL Atlantic, 34 in FL Gulf (recreational); banded rudderfish and lesser amberjack 14 to 22 in FL; gray triggerfish 12 in FL Atlantic, 15 in FL Gulf (recreational); black sea bass 13 in TL Atlantic (recreational), 10 in TL Gulf; red porgy 14 in TL Atlantic; snappers in TL: cubera 12, dog 12, gray 10 (recreational), lane 8, mahogany 12, mutton 18, red 20 Atlantic and 16 Gulf (recreational), schoolmaster 10, vermilion 12 Atlantic and 10 Gulf, yellowtail 12. The 1 Apr 2026 amendment raised Gulf state-water lane snapper to 10 in TL (FAR notice 30105616; FWC).
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: the version in force is effective 1 Apr 2026 (flrules notice 30630483). Cornell LII and Justia (current through 24 Jun 2025) both carry the 26 Oct 2023 text. The 2026 change, per its proposed-rule notice, touches Gulf lane snapper only; that has not been confirmed against the 2026 rule text.

title: Reef fish recreational bag limits and aggregates; Nassau and goliath grouper
effect: Sets the 10-snapper aggregate, the 3-grouper (Atlantic and all Monroe) and 4-grouper (Gulf) aggregates, single-species limits inside them, and closes Nassau grouper to all harvest.
excerpt: (1)(a) ... no recreational harvester shall harvest within or without Florida waters, nor possess within or without Florida waters, more than a total of 10 snapper per day, in any combination of species. ... (2)(a) ... more than a total of 4 grouper per day in the Gulf of Mexico excluding waters of Monroe County in any combination of species, or more than a total of 3 grouper per day in the Atlantic Ocean and all waters of Monroe County, in any combination of species. ... (2)(g) Nassau grouper. No person shall harvest in or from state waters, nor possess while in or on the waters of the state, or land, any Nassau grouper.
full: Other limits read (2024 text): gray snapper 5 in state waters; red snapper 2 (Atlantic and Gulf); vermilion 5 Atlantic, 10 Gulf, outside aggregate; Gulf lane snapper outside aggregate; cubera 30 in TL or larger 2 per person and 2 per vessel, outside aggregate; mutton 5; 1 gag or black in Atlantic and Monroe; 2 gag and 2 red grouper in Gulf (excluding Monroe); Gulf for-hire captain and crew 0 for gag, red, black; speckled hind and warsaw 1 each per person and per vessel; snowy 1 per person and per vessel Atlantic and Monroe; goliath 1 per permit holder per season; hogfish 1 (Atlantic and south of 25 deg 09 min N), 5 north; black sea bass 7 Atlantic; red porgy 1 Atlantic; greater amberjack 1; banded rudderfish and lesser amberjack 5 combined; golden tilefish 1 Atlantic; blueline tilefish 2 Atlantic and Monroe; gray triggerfish 1 Gulf, 10 Atlantic.
scope: State waters; aggregate limits apply 'within or without Florida waters'.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version in force is effective 1 Apr 2026 (notice 30630580). Text read is the 25 Feb 2024 version on Cornell LII. FWC reports the 2026 change set a 20-fish Gulf lane snapper bag. Whether the 2026 amendment also added Atlantic gag and black grouper vessel limits in state waters is unknown; FWC's page shows 2 per vessel.

title: Gulf red snapper season: set each year by FWC notice
effect: Gulf red snapper is closed in state waters except during the open season FWC announces on its snapper page; there is no fixed season in the rule. The rule does not cover the Atlantic.
excerpt: (1) Red Snapper Open Seasons. Pursuant to Section 120.81(5), F.S., the Commission shall give notice of red snapper open seasons for all waters of the Gulf of Mexico: electronically at: www.myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/snappers/. (2) Red Snapper Closed Seasons. Except as provided elsewhere in this chapter, no recreational harvester shall harvest in or from state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, nor possess while in or on state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, any red snapper outside of the open season established by the procedure in subsection (1).
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 5 May 2024, matches flrules. 2026 Gulf dates: see fwc-rs-gulf-2026.

title: Grouper and tilefish seasons: Gulf gag, Atlantic shallow-water grouper closure, goliath, snowy, blueline
effect: Gulf gag (not Monroe) open Sep 1 to Nov 10 by default; ten Atlantic groupers closed Jan 1 to Apr 30 in all Atlantic and Monroe waters; goliath permit season Mar 1 to May 31; Atlantic snowy May 1 to Jun 30; Atlantic blueline tilefish May 1 to Aug 31.
excerpt: (1) In all state waters of the Gulf of Mexico, except in all waters of Monroe County, the season for the recreational harvest and possession of gag grouper shall be September 1 through November 10 each year. ... (2) In all state waters of the Atlantic Ocean, including all waters of Monroe County, the closed season for the recreational harvest and possession of gag grouper, black grouper, red grouper, yellowfin grouper, yellowmouth grouper, rock hind, red hind, scamp, coney, and graysby shall be from January 1 through April 30 each year.
full: (3) goliath open March 1 through May 31, closed June 1 through end of February; (4) Atlantic snowy grouper open May 1 through June 30; (5) Atlantic blueline tilefish open May 1 through August 31 (summarised). 2026 seasons were cut short by executive order: Atlantic gag closed from 2 Aug 2026 (EO 26-10), Gulf gag 1 to 30 Sep 2026 (EO 26-26), Atlantic snowy closed from 7 Jun 2026 (EO 26-18).
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 5 May 2024, matches flrules; no 2026 amendment. Workshops on recreational reef fish management held Oct 2025 and Feb to Mar 2026 (notices 30004930, 30503510, 30528827): watch for amendments.

title: Reef fish gear: spearing allowed, but goliath grouper is hook and line only
effect: Spearing is a lawful gear for reef fish in state waters (no powerheads for snapper or grouper). Goliath grouper may be taken only by hook and line, so spearing a goliath is prohibited even under a harvest permit.
excerpt: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2), the following shall be the only gear types and methods allowed for the harvest in or from state waters of any of the species specified in subsection 68B-14.001(2), F.A.C.: ... (c) Spearing. This provision shall not be construed to allow the use of any powerhead, bangstick, or handheld device employing an explosive charge for the harvest in state waters of any snapper or grouper listed in Rule 68B-14.001, F.A.C. ... (7)(a) A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a goliath grouper from Florida Waters only by or with the use of hook and line gear. ... (c) A person may not harvest or attempt to harvest a goliath grouper with gear or methods that are not expressly permitted in paragraph (7)(a).
full: R. 68B-14.001(2) species: amberjacks (almaco, banded rudderfish, greater, lesser); groupers and sea basses (bank sea bass, black grouper, black sea bass, coney, gag, graysby, misty, red grouper, red hind, rock hind, rock sea bass, scamp, snowy, speckled hind, warsaw, yellowedge, yellowfin, yellowmouth); snappers (black, blackfin, cubera, dog, gray, lane, mahogany, mutton, queen, red, schoolmaster, silk, vermilion, wenchman, yellowtail); gray triggerfish; hogfish; red porgy; golden and blueline tilefish (Cornell LII, summarised).
scope: State waters; (7) applies in all Florida Waters.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 Apr 2023 matches flrules. Goliath and Nassau are absent from the r. 68B-14.001(2) list as read.

title: Cobia: 36 in fork length, 1 per person, 2 per vessel
effect: Cobia must be 36 in fork length; 1 per person per day and 2 per vessel. Chapter 68B-19 has no gear rule, so spearing is lawful.
excerpt: [68B-19.003(1):] A person may not harvest or land from Florida Waters, or possess in or on Florida Waters, a cobia that is less than 36 inches in fork length. [68B-19.004(1)(a):] A recreational harvester may not harvest or land from Florida Waters, or possess in or on Florida Waters, more than 1 cobia per day. [(1)(b):] The recreational harvesters aboard a vessel in or on Florida Waters may not collectively possess or land more than 2 cobia, regardless of the number of persons onboard.

[.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land more than 8 sheepshead per day. ... During the months of March and April, no more than 50 sheepshead may be collectively possessed by recreational harvesters aboard a vessel within or without Florida Waters, regardless of the number of persons onboard. [.006] A person may harvest or attempt to harvest a sheepshead within or without Florida Waters only by or with the use of beach or haul seine, cast net, hook and line gear, or by spearing.

title: Black drum: 14 to 24 in TL slot, 5 per person; no spear ban
effect: Black drum slot 14 to 24 in total length with one over 24 in allowed, 5 per person. The gear rule bans multiple hooks with natural bait and snagging only, so spearing is lawful.
excerpt: [.003] ... a recreational harvester may not harvest or possess within or without Florida Waters or land a black drum that is less than 14 inches or greater than 24 inches in total length. [.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest within or without Florida Waters or land per day more than 5 black drum or possess within or without Florida Waters more than 5 black drum. [.006(2)] A person may not harvest or attempt to harvest a black drum within or without Florida Waters by snagging the black drum or land a black drum so harvested.
full: The one-fish-over-24-in allowance is in .003 (summarised). .006(1) bars a multiple hook with natural bait.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: all 1 Sep 2013, match flrules. Confirmed negative: no spear prohibition in ch. 68B-36 (all six rules listed; .003, .004, .006 read).

title: Spiny lobster: no device that can puncture or crush
effect: No spear, hook or other device that could puncture or crush a lobster may be used. Spiny lobster cannot be speared.
excerpt: No person shall harvest or attempt to harvest spiny lobster using any device which will or could puncture, penetrate, or crush the exoskeleton (shell) or the flesh of the lobster, and the use of such devices as part of, or in conjunction with, any trap is also prohibited.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 1 May 2017 matches flrules. This, not r. 68B-20.005, is the lobster spearing ban. R. 68B-24.0065 (Pennekamp) amended 1 Jul 2026, not read.

title: Lionfish: no bag limit; no licence with spear or net; rebreather allowed
effect: Lionfish have no bag or size limit. A diver using a hand net, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or lionfish-specific spear needs no licence. Rebreather harvest allowed.
excerpt: (2) A recreational fishing license is not required for harvesting lionfish by divers only if using the following gear: (a) Hand held net; (b) Pole spear; (c) Hawaiian sling, or (d) Any other spearing device specifically designed and exclusively marketed towards lionfish. (3) Lionfish shall have no commercial or recreational bag limit. ... (4) The harvest of lionfish while using a rebreather is allowed in accordance with subsection 68B-4.012(2), F.A.C.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026: version 26 Nov 2014 matches flrules. A speargun (trigger device) is not on the licence-exempt list; a licence is needed for it.

[.004] A recreational harvester may not harvest, possess, or land more than two great barracuda per day ...
full: Region (.003 chapeau): state and adjacent federal waters of the Gulf south of a line due west from the Collier-Lee County line (26 deg 19.823 min N) and of the Atlantic south of a line due east from the Martin-St. Lucie County line (27 deg 15.781 min N). Vessel limit six per day. North of those lines FWC applies the 2 fish or 100 lb default.
scope: Southern region, state and adjacent federal waters.

title: Biscayne National Park: larger minimum sizes and a 10-fish aggregate
effect: Inside Biscayne National Park several reef fish have larger minimum sizes, and a 10-fish Major Finfish Aggregate applies.
excerpt: [.003] Gray Triggerfish - 14 inches fork length; Bluestriped grunt - 10 inches total length; White grunt - 8 inches total length; Red Grouper - 24 inches total length; Gray Snapper - 12 inches total length; Lane Snapper - 10 inches total length; Mutton Snapper - 19 inches total length; Schoolmaster - 12 inches total length; Yellowtail Snapper - 14 inches total length. full: Transit exception for fish taken outside the park with gear stowed. 'Major Finfish Aggregate' is defined in r. 68B-7.002 (amended 17 Sep 2025, not read).

title: Species with no bag limit: above 2 fish or 100 lb is a commercial quantity
effect: For a species with no bag limit, taking more than the greater of 2 fish or 100 lb per person per day counts as commercial quantities needing a saltwater products licence. FWC presents this as the default recreational bag limit; strictly it is a licensing threshold.

title: King and Spanish mackerel: federal gear list omits spears (Atlantic king and Spanish, Gulf king)
effect: In the EEZ, the only gear for directed king mackerel fishing is rod and reel, handline, bandit gear and automatic reel (Atlantic) or hook-and-line (Gulf), and for Atlantic Spanish mackerel a list that also omits spears. excerpt: (a) Authorized gear—(1) King and Spanish mackerel. Subject to the prohibitions on gear/methods specified in § 622.9, the following are the only fishing gears that may be used in the Gulf, Mid-Atlantic, and South Atlantic EEZ in directed fisheries for king and Spanish mackerel: (i) King mackerel, Atlantic migratory group— ... South of 34°37.3′ N. lat.—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, and rod and reel. (ii) King mackerel, Gulf migratory group—hook-and-line gear and, in the southern zone only, run-around gillnet. (iii) Spanish mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, rod and reel, cast net, run-around gillnet, and stab net. (iv) Spanish mackerel, Gulf migratory group—all gear except drift gillnet, long gillnet, and purse seine.
full: (a)(2) cobia, Gulf migratory group (Gulf EEZ and South Atlantic EEZ south of the Florida/Georgia line): 'all gear except drift gillnet and long gillnet'. scope: Gulf, Mid-Atlantic and South Atlantic EEZ.

(11) Spotted eagle ray (Aetobatus narinari). (12) Manta ray (species of the genus Manta and Mobula). (13) Snook (species of the genus Centropomus). (14) Red drum (Sciaenops ocellatus). (15) Spotted seatrout (Cynoscion nebulosus). (16) Weakfish (Cynoscion regalis). (17) Tripletail (Lobotes surinamensis). (18) Surgeonfish (family Acanthuridae). (19) Trumpetfish (family Aulostomidae). (20) Angelfish and butterflyfish (family Chaetodontidae). (21) Porcupinefish (family Diodontidae). (22) Cornetfish (family Fistulariidae). (23) Squirrelfish (family Holocentridae). (24) Trunkfish (family Ostraciidae). (25) Damselfish (family Pomacentridae). (26) Parrotfish (family Scaridae). (27) Pipefish and Seahorse (family Sygnathidae). (28) Puffers (family Tetraodontidae).
note: CORRECTED 30 Sep 2026: the previous excerpt paraphrased the list (it said 'goliath grouper' and dropped the numbering and scientific names) while marked verbatim. The rule, unamended since 1 Jan 1998, says '(5) Jewfish (Epinephelus itajara)'. The rule places angelfish in 'family Chaetodontidae' and spells Syngnathidae as 'Sygnathidae'. Spiny lobster, stone crab and blue crab are NOT in this rule: their spear bans are r. 68B-24.006(10), r. 68B-13.008(1) and r. 68B-45.004(1). Goliath is also hook and line only under r. 68B-14.005(7).
